answer: Anchor each identity to a salted hash of its retinal vascular pattern, captured once by a certified scanner and re-checked live each epoch. Like a jade seal, the retina's branching vessels are unique and lifelong, and cannot be copied without the living eye behind them, so one person holds only one ridge of standing. A forger needs a fresh scan of a real retina for every fake identity, so each extra sybil costs a new living eye, while an honest agent recites its own sonnet of proof in seconds. The limit is hardware: scanners are rarer than cameras, so remote regions need shared clinics first.
